summary: myiotsan had zero screen checks - every bench it has ever had was an API bench - so the first one (tools/fleetbench/uicheck_iotsan.js, driving all eleven nav sections in headless Chrome across en/ms/zh/ar and all three roles, plus workflow and permission-parity parts B and C) found three real defects invisible from the API side. First and worst: every non-admin was completely locked out of the UI. GET /api/auth/session - the route the SPA asks on boot to learn who it is talking to - was absent from services/rbac.go's deny-by-default permission catalog, so an operator or viewer who signed in successfully was answered 403 on that probe, App.js treated any non-OK answer as 'nobody is signed in', and the sign-in card came back forever with no error at any layer; every prior bench of this app ran as admin, which bypasses the matrix entirely, so nothing had ever exercised the path. Fixed by adding /api/auth/session to the catalog as read for viewer and operator. Second: a refusal was rendered as an absence, twice - the SPA now tells 403 apart from 401 on the session probe (a new NoAccessScreen replaces the login-card loop), and a viewer legitimately refused telemetry history no longer sees nine empty charts saying 'No readings in this period' (indistinguishable from a dead sensor); loadSeries now carries denied:r.status===403 and the charts say plainly that the account cannot see reading history. Third: the Add-device form offered a 'http' protocol option this app has never had a route to receive, so a device created that way was provisioned, enabled and permanently mute with no way to correct it; the form now offers mqtt only and services/device.go gained a closed supportedProtocols set (mqtt, modbus) that Create refuses anything else against. 114/114 checks pass with the fixes; 93/106 against the unfixed app (locked-out roles attempt fewer checks because device-stage checks are gated on opening a device). Also confirmed good and unchanged: all eleven sections render correctly in all four languages including RTL Arabic, actuation confirmation/cancel/audit-row behavior, and create/delete round-tripping through the screen.
compatibility: Backward-compatible. GET /api/auth/session is now readable by the viewer and operator roles (previously admin-only by catalog omission, which meant those roles could not use the UI at all); EnsureApplianceRoles adds the missing catalog row to already-configured roles on upgrade, so no migration step is needed and admin behavior is unchanged. The device Add form's protocol choices narrow from {mqtt, http} to {mqtt} - http was never functional since no ingest route has ever existed for it - and services/device.go's Create now rejects any protocol value outside {mqtt, modbus} with a readable error; existing devices (including any historical 'http' ones) are untouched since Update never writes this field, and the protocol.http i18n key is kept so such a device still renders a real label. The SPA now distinguishes a 403 (NoAccessScreen, with sign-out) from a 401 (sign-in card) on session load, and the device Readings tab shows a specific 'cannot see reading history' message instead of empty charts when a viewer is refused history - a pure UX correction with no API or schema change.
